artifacts.title: Lebo v. Susquehanna Valley Presbytery

matches.evidence: 1997-17 — Lebo v. Susquehanna Valley Presbytery Court: Standing Judicial Commission · Assembly: 27th (1999) · Disposition: denied Source: [ga27_1999 pp. 77–79](../markdown/ga27_1999.md ga27-p77)

The Complainant argued that the congregation should not have input on this decision, that only the Session has the authority to make a decision such as this. He argued that BCO 12-5b grants the Session the right "to approve and adopt the budget."

In this instance, we do not find that there was a violation of BCO 12-5b with regard to the Session's power to approve and adopt the budget. The issue before the congregation was not whether to approve or not to approve the budget or any portion of
the budget (and thus contradict BCO 12-5b). In this case, sufficient safeguards, denial

artifacts.synopsis: Dennis Lebo complained that Susquehanna Valley Presbytery erred in denying his complaint that the congregation of Carlisle Reformed Presbyterian Church acted unconstitutionally when it voted to supplement the Assistant Pastor's Fund. The SJC denied the complaint, finding that the congregation's action did not violate BCO 12-5b because the Session retained authority to approve and adopt the final budget.

artifacts.title: Session authority over church budget versus congregational call terms

matches.evidence: The CCB answered yes: under BCO 12-5.b, the session's duty to approve the budget supersedes the congregation's authority to set pastoral call terms in any fiscal year.

artifacts.title: Session authority to approve ministerial severance packages

matches.evidence: CCB advised that sessions may approve severance packages for ministers without congregational approval, as these are budgetary matters under BCO 12-5b.

artifacts.title: Session's right to access congregation's financial and attendance records

matches.evidence: CCB advised that the session and diaconate have a right to access financial and attendance records as needed, limited only by prudence and protection of reputation.

artifacts.title: Disqualifying same-sex attracted men from ordination under BCO 7

matches.evidence: An overture from Westminster Presbytery to amend BCO 7 and related provisions disqualifying same-sex attracted men from ordination was found in conflict and adopted.

artifacts.title: Ordination ban for men self-identifying as gay Christians

matches.evidence: The CCB found this overture to amend BCO 17 prohibiting ordination of men using gay-identity labels to be in conflict with existing BCO provisions, though it was adopted.
